fatal_errors: The hypothesis does not identify the refractory Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W design space or the brittle equimolar NbMoTaVW baseline.
It replaces the target's composition-screening strategy based on VEC, rule-of-mixtures modulus, and density with an unsupported 1–3 at.% Ti precipitation strategy.
The proposed dual-phase mediator directly conflicts with the demonstrated single-phase BCC designed alloy.
The claimed percentage improvements in strength, modulus, ductility, and fracture toughness have no cited or supplied evidence.
The proposed tests and processing conditions do not reconstruct the as-cast, room-temperature, quasi-static compression validation used in the target study.
explanation: The response is aligned only at the broad level of seeking improved mechanical-property combinations in structural HEAs. It misses the central methodology: validation of composition-based modulus estimates, screening 38,326 Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W compositions, minimizing VEC while retaining modulus, and selecting Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5. Its phase-separation mechanism is contrary to the observed single-phase BCC structure and omits the proposed VEC-dependent reduction of the Peierls–Nabarro barrier, enhanced dislocation mobility, slip, delayed cracking, and work hardening. It also fails to recover the measured outcome of 35.7% compressive fracture strain, 1115 MPa yield strength, and 2550 MPa compressive strength relative to the approximately 2% strain and 1246 MPa yield-strength baseline. The paired-control experiment is directionally testable, but the baseline alloy, heat treatment, phase criteria, statistical plan, and specimen standards are insufficiently specified. Moreover, absence of a dual phase and absence of property improvement are treated interchangeably even though they test different links in the causal hypothesis. With no supporting evidence and arbitrary numerical forecasts, this is not a well-supported plausible alternative.
